glosses: Free of flaws or imperfections; unsullied.

examples.text: Such was the origin of a friendship as warm and pure as any that ancient or modern history records.

glosses: Free of foreign material or pollutants.

examples.text: A guinea is pure gold if it has in it no alloy.
As for the rest, the air here is said to be purer than elsewhere in Ireland; the water of the Nore is beautifully transparent; and the bogless state of the land helps out the rhyme.
"Hetch Hetchy water is the purest, wholly unpolluted, and forever unpollutable."

glosses: Free of immoral behavior or qualities; clean.

examples.text: Laye hondes sodenly on no man nether be part taker of wother mens synnes. Kepe thy silfe pure.
That idea is pure madness!

glosses: Done for its own sake instead of serving another branch of science.

examples.text: The [Isaac] Newton that emerges from the [unpublished] manuscripts is far from the popular image of a rational practitioner of cold and pure reason. The architect of modern science was himself not very modern. He was obsessed with alchemy.

glosses: Of a single, simple sound or tone; said of some vowels and the unaspirated consonants.
Without harmonics or overtones; not harsh or discordant.

examples.text: Well when ah's youngah, ah'd just light a candle rahn de dinna table play pure crazy 8s and spades vif my brotha til we lot dozed off...

glosses: to a great extent or degree; extremely; exceedingly.

examples.text: You’re pure busy.
I just get pure shy with the interview cats.

glosses: To hit (the ball) completely cleanly and accurately.

examples.text: Tiger Woods pured his first drive straight down the middle of the fairway.

glosses: One who, or that which, is pure.

examples.text: ... the establishment of an inferior College, and the consequent connexion of the many thousands of British practitioners in medicine and surgery with a subordinate institution, and one that should be subservient to the government of the pures.

glosses: Alternative form of puer (“dung (e.g. of dogs)”).

examples.text: […] Dogs'-dung is called ‘Pure’, from its cleansing and purifying properties.

Mary smelled the rancid odor of the tannery on the right side of the road.[…]
"What is that, Mary?" Jake asked.
"'Tis a bag for collecting pure. That is going to be your job, Jake. You are to collect pure."
"Pure? What is pure?"

translations.source_sense_description: Metall: in elementarer Form (nicht als Erz) vorkommend

glosses: That can be picked up or held, having a texture, and usually firm. Unlike a liquid, gas or plasma.

examples.text: Almost all metals are solid at room temperature.

glosses: Large in size, quantity, or value.

examples.text: Almost a quarter of a million copies is really a solid number for today's record industry. In fact, that number is more than the last two number one albums
Americans increased their borrowing by a solid amount in September. But the gain was less than half the big August surge
On top of that, the speaker is big, so you may have to set aside a solid amount of space for it.

glosses: Lacking holes, hollows or admixtures of other materials.

solid chocolate

a solid foundation

glosses: Qualifie des personnes, en parlant de la ville, du lieu où elles ont pris naissance, et suppose ordinairement l’établissement fixe des parents, l’éducation, etc. ; à la différence de né qui peut supposer seulement la naissance accidentelle.

Il est natif de Paris, de Lyon. - Elle est native de Rouen.

examples.text: C’est un homme très sérieux.

Air, maintien sérieux.

examples.text: Il était sérieux, c’est-à-dire, pour un ouvrier, ni feignant, ni buveur, ni noceur.

Cet homme n’a rien de sérieux dans le caractère.

glosses: Qui est crédible ou digne de confiance.

examples.text: Nous souhaitons que vous trouviez un fournisseur sérieux pouvant fabriquer dans les délais voulus et à des conditions avantageuses pour l’État.
